Kākinī
------------------------------------------
Yoginīs are a group of female deities, 64 in number, associated with दुर्गा. काकिनी is one of them. She is generally pictured as having four faces, three eyes and two or four hands. Decorated in yellow garments, she is shown as having a skull-bowl in one hand and exhibiting the abhayamudrā (gesture of protection) with the other. In the case of four hands, they carry in addition, a noose and show the varadamudrā (boon-giving posture). She is sometimes posited as the presiding goddess of the अनाहतचक्र (lotus of the heart).

Kākabhuṣuṇḍi
------------------------------------------
Kākabhuṣuṇḍi is an old wise sage in the form of a crow.
The incident of his teaching the story of Śrī राम in brief, to गरुड, the eagle-mount of विष्णु, is recorded in the Rāmacaritamānasa (Uttarakāṇḍa, dohas 64 to 68) of तुलसीदास (A.

-1622).
When राम and लक्ष्मण were bound by the नागपाश (weapon of snakes that binds) of इन्द्रजित् and became unconscious, गरुड arrived and saved them (vide the Rāmāyaṇa of वाल्मीकि, Yuddha-kāṇḍa,

to 50).
Seeing राम in that pathetic condition, गरुड started doubting his divinity. To clear this, he went to the sage नारद who directed him to ब्रह्मा, the creator, ब्रह्मा in turn sent him to शिव who again advised him to go to the sage काकभुषुण्डि.
Kākabhuṣuṇḍi received him with warmth and affection, and made him to listen to the story of राम which he was about to narrate to the birds that had gathered there. By devotedly listening to the story, गरुड’s doubts were cleared and his faith in राम was restored.
Later काकभुषुण्डि also describes his adventures as a baby crow with the child राम.
